Blessed
blĕs'ed
adj. & pple. (made happy by God; also worthy to be praised; rendering Hebrew ashre, baruk, Greek makarios, eulogetos)
From Saxon bletsian, to consecrate, anciently connected with blood and the hallowing of an altar. The English word carries two distinct originals in Scripture, and confusing them is the commonest error in reading it.

Biblical Definition

Blessed translates two different words and points in two different directions, and Scripture never mixes them. When God is the object, the sense is worthy to be praised: “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ” (Ephesians 1:3). Paul is not wishing God well; he is ascribing what is already His, and the same verse then turns the other direction — God blesses us, and the blessings named are spiritual and located in Christ, not in circumstance. Paul carries the ascription further and calls Him “the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords” (1 Timothy 6:15). When man is the object, the sense is happy under God's favour, and the Psalter opens with it as a description of a settled life: “Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful” (Psalm 1:1). The blessedness is defined first by what the man refuses. Our Lord takes the same form and drives it to the place no natural reading would go: “Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven” (Matthew 5:3). The blessing is announced over the bankrupt, and the reason given is possession of a kingdom — which is to say blessedness in Scripture is a verdict from heaven upon a man, not a report on his conditions.

Webster 1828 Definition

Made happy or prosperous by God's favour; and, when applied to God, worthy of adoration and praise. Psalm 1 and the Beatitudes both define the blessed man by his relation to God rather than by his circumstances.

expand to see more

BLESSED, pp. Made happy or prosperous; extolled; pronounced happy.

2. a. Happy; prosperous in worldly affairs; enjoying spiritual happiness and the favor of God. Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly. Ps. 1.

3. Happy in heavenly enjoyment; as the blessed in heaven.

4. Worthy of adoration; holy; as the blessed God; the blessed and only Potentate. 1 Tim. 6.

5. It is used in the phrase blessed be, as an ascription of praise, and in blessed are, as a declaration of the happy state of those described. Blessed are the poor in spirit. Mat. 5.

Key Scripture

Psalm 1:1 — "Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful."

Matthew 5:3 — "Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven."

Ephesians 1:3 — "Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ:"

1 Timothy 6:15 — "Which in his times he shall shew, who is the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords;"

Modern Corruption

Blessed has been reduced to a caption for good fortune — the house, the health, the raise — which makes the Beatitudes unreadable, since they pronounce blessing on the poor, the mourning, and the persecuted.

expand to see more

The word now functions as a tag attached to visible advantage, and the effect is to make blessing evidence. If a man is blessed because his circumstances are favourable, then unfavourable circumstances are evidence of the withdrawal of favour, and the whole apparatus of the prosperity teaching follows by simple logic. Scripture destroys the premise in the first sentence of the Sermon on the Mount. “Blessed are the poor in spirit” is not a promise that the poor in spirit will soon be rich in spirit; it is a declaration that theirs is the kingdom of heaven, present tense, in the condition described. Job in the ash heap is blessed. Paul in the Mamertine is blessed. The Lord Himself, having nowhere to lay His head, is the blessed and only Potentate's beloved Son, and the caption would not have fit Him for a single day of His ministry.

The recovery is to hear the word as a verdict rather than a description. Psalm 1 begins by naming three things the blessed man does not do — he does not walk, stand, or sit with the ungodly, the sinner, and the scorner — and only then says what he delights in. Blessedness is bound to a settled relation to God's law and a settled separation from the counsel of the ungodly, neither of which shows in a photograph. Ephesians 1:3 locates the blessings precisely: all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ. That is where they are kept, and it is why they cannot be lost in a market crash or a diagnosis. A believer who learns to say blessed be God before he says I am blessed has the two senses in the right order, and the second will stop lying to him.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew ashre (happy, blessed — of man) and barak / baruk (to kneel, to bless — chiefly of God); Greek makarios (blessed, happy — of man) and eulogetos (well-spoken-of, worthy of praise — of God).

expand to see more

Hebrew ashre (H835) — happiness, blessedness of a man; the opening word of the Psalter, “Blessed is the man” (Psalm 1:1).

Hebrew barak (H1288) — to kneel, and so to bless; used both of God blessing man and of man blessing God in adoration.

Greek makarios (G3107) — blessed, happy; the word repeated nine times in the Beatitudes (Matthew 5:3-11).

Greek eulogetos (G2128) — worthy to be praised, blessed; used in the New Testament of God alone, as in Ephesians 1:3.

Greek eulogeo (G2127) — to speak well of, bless; the verb behind “hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings.”

Usage

"“Blessed be the God and Father” — ascription to God of what is already His."

"“Blessed are the poor in spirit” — the verdict pronounced over the bankrupt, in the condition described."

"“All spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ” — the location of the believer's blessing, safe from circumstance."
